title: Gacha System
summary: Defines acquisition purpose, rarities, banners, pity, guarantees, duplicates, free acquisition and transparency without making random pulls mandatory for core content.

blocks.text: Character acquisition, banners, pity, and guarantees

The Gacha system in Symphony of Justice functions primarily as a character and weapon acquisition system, while also serving as one of the components that can support the project’s continued expansion. It is not the core of the gameplay experience.
The Core Loop must remain complete even during a session in which the player does not interact with any Banner.
EXPLORE → FIGHT → OBTAIN → IMPROVE → BUILD A TEAM
must remain a complete experience independently of the Gacha system.
This is consistent with the Game Vision, where Gacha is defined as an acquisition and distribution system rather than a Game Pillar.
The Game Vision also establishes that strategy must not depend exclusively on spending and that limited characters should never be mandatory to complete required content.
The system serves five primary functions:
Allows the player to obtain new characters and selected weapons.
Provides long-term goals for players interested in building a broad roster.

However, monetization should fund the experience, not deliberately create problems and then sell the solution.
What Must Never Depend on Random Chance
The player should never depend on a random pull in order to:
have access to basic combat roles;
obtain an element that is indispensable for a mandatory puzzle.
Historical exploration documentation already expresses a similar principle by recognizing that it would be unjustifiable to lock basic content behind ownership of a specialized character.
Gacha expands the player’s possibilities. It does not grant permission to play.
The Gacha system should clearly separate the different acquisition categories so that players understand what they are trying to obtain.
Historical documentation already separates characters and weapons, and later introduces thematic Banners.
Characters are the primary collectible content.
No character should require their promotional weapon for the basic kit to function correctly.
I do not recommend placing skins inside the main Gacha pool.
Historical documentation already treats clothing and skins as separate commercial products.
This is cleaner for the player.

The player knows exactly what they are purchasing.

No Paying to Solve Designed Frustration
artificial difficulty tied to the current Banner;
bosses that are practically immune without the newest character;
nerfing older characters to promote new ones;
pity loss when a Banner ends without clear notice.
The Game Vision explicitly establishes that characters should not lose value rapidly and that important content should not become practically impossible without limited units.
Do not design characters whose reasonable power level begins only at Legacy VI.
Before commercial launch, the project must review:
The player should know what can be obtained, the maximum cost before a guarantee, and what happens if the featured result is not obtained.
The Game Vision already establishes that the Core Gameplay Prototype does not require a functional Gacha system, shop, or microtransactions.
